title: A Study of Anakinra in Japanese Patients With Still's Disease (SJIA and AOSD)
off: A Randomized, Double-blind, Placebo-controlled, Multicenter, Phase 3 Efficacy and Safety Study of Subcutaneous Anakinra in Japanese Patients With Still's Disease (SJIA and AOSD)
summary: A study to demonstrate efficacy and safety of anakinra in pediatric and adult Japanese patients with Still's disease (Systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis \[SJIA\] and Adult-onset Still's disease \[AOSD\]).
desc:
The study consists of two phases:

• Core phase comprising 2 weeks double blind placebo-controlled treatment, 52 weeks open label treatment and 4 weeks safety follow up (only for patients not entering the extension phase).

At the Week 54 visit, patients who consent and are eligible to continue anakinra treatment, will enter the extension phase and continue open label anakinra treatment.

• Extension phase comprising up to 26 weeks open label treatment and 4 weeks safety follow up.

The primary endpoint will be evaluated at Week 2 visit.
elig:
Key Inclusion Criteria:

1. Male and female patients, 8 months of age or older with a body weight ≥ 10 kg
2. Diagnosis of Still's disease
3. If \< 16 years of age at disease onset, the diagnosis is madeaccording to adapted ILAR criteria i.e., CARRA criteria for SJIA. If ≥ 16 years of age at disease onset, the diagnosis is made according to Yamaguchi criteria for AOSD.
4. Active disease confirmed by the following three signs and symptoms. a. Active arthritis in ≥ 1 joint. b. CRP \> 30 mg/L. c. At least one fever episode (≥ 38.0 degree Celsius) attributable to the disease within one week before enrollment.
5. The result of tuberculosis test within 8 weeks prior to enrollment is negative.

Key Exclusion Criteria:

1. Previous or current treatment with anakinra, or any other Interleukin-1 (IL-1) inhibitor except for canakinumab. Previous treatment with canakinumab is allowed if canakinumab was discontinued for reasons other than lack of efficacy and after a washout period of minimum 130 days. Patients who have discontinued canakinumab because of insufficient effect or refractory disease are not allowed to be enrolled in the study.
2. Use of the following therapies prior to enrollment.

   1. Narcotic analgesics within 24 hours prior to enrollment.
   2. Diaminodiphenyl sulfone within 1 week prior to enrollment or etanercept within 2 weeks prior to enrollment.
   3. Intraarticular, intramuscular, or intravenous administration of glucocorticoids within 72h(3 days) prior to enrollment, or intravenous immunoglobulin within 4 weeks prior to enrollment.
   4. Intravenous immunoglobulins with proven Still's disease modifying effect, leflunomide, infliximab, or adalimumab within 8 weeks prior to enrollment.
   5. Thalidomide within 72h(3 days) prior to enrollment, cyclosporine within 5 weeks prior to enrollment, mycophenolate mofetil within 1 week prior to enrollment, 6-mercaptopurine within 48h(2 days) prior to enrollment, azathioprine within 72h(3 days) prior to enrollment, cyclophosphamide within 96h(4 days) prior to enrollment, chlorambucil (not approved inJapan) within 48h(2 days) prior to enrollment, or any other immunosuppressants within 12 weeks prior to enrollment.
   6. Tocilizumab within 4 weeks prior to enrollment or any other immunomodulatory medications within 4 half-lives prior to enrollment.
   7. Rituximab within 13 weeks prior to enrollment.
   8. Canakinumab within 130 days prior to enrollment
3. Live vaccines within 4 weeks prior to enrollment.
4. Known presence or suspicion of active, chronic, or recurrent bacterial, fungal, or viral infections, including but not limited to tuberculosis, HIV infection, Covid-19 infection, or hepatitis B or C infection at baseline. Patients with acute or chronic HBV.
5. Clinical evidence of liver disease or liver injury as indicated by presence of abnormal liver tests.
6. Presence of severe chronic kidney disease (CKD) grades 4 and 5.
7. Presence of neutropenia (absolute neutrophil count \[ANC\] \< 1.5 x 10\^9/L).
8. Presence of thrombocytopenia (platelets count \< 100 x 10\^9/L).
9. Presence or suspicion of MAS at baseline.
10. History or diagnosis of MAS within the last 4 weeks prior to enrollment.

After completion of the study Core Phase, patients who consent and are eligible to continue anakinra treatment, can enter the extension phase .

arms.d: 100 mg/day or 2 mg/kg/day of subcutaneous anakinra for those with a body weight ≥50 kg or \<50 kg, respectively.
Corresponding volume to 100 mg/day or 2 mg/kg/day

primary.m: An improvement of ≥ 30% from baseline in physician global assessment of disease activity (visual analogue scale [VAS]).
An improvement of ≥ 30% from baseline in patient/parent global assessment of overall well-being (VAS).
An improvement of ≥ 30% from baseline in number of joints with active arthritis.
An improvement of ≥ 30% from baseline in number of joints with limitation of motion.
An improvement of ≥ 30% from baseline in assessment of physical function: Child health assessment questionnaire (CHAQ)/Stanford health assessment questionnaire (SHAQ).
An improvement of ≥ 30% from baseline in C-reactive protein (CRP) (mg/L).

x.titre: Anakinra chez des patients japonais atteints de maladie de Still (AJIs et Still de l'adulte)
x.question: L'anakinra sous-cutané est-il efficace et bien toléré, par rapport au placebo, chez des patients japonais atteints de maladie de Still ?
x.contexte:
La maladie de Still regroupe l'arthrite juvénile idiopathique systémique (AJIs) et la maladie de Still de l'adulte. C'est une maladie auto-inflammatoire rare, avec fièvre, éruption, arthrite et inflammation biologique, exposant au syndrome d'activation macrophagique. Le traitement repose sur les corticoïdes, les anti-IL-1 et les anti-IL-6.

L'anakinra est un antagoniste recombinant du récepteur de l'IL-1, utilisé de longue date dans ces maladies en Europe et aux États-Unis. Au Japon, son accès dans cette indication reste limité, d'où le besoin de données locales.

Cette étude de phase 3 du promoteur Swedish Orphan Biovitrum est randomisée en quadruple insu. Elle inclut environ 15 patients japonais d'au moins 8 mois et de 10 kg ou plus. La phase centrale comprend 2 semaines contre placebo, puis 52 semaines d'anakinra en ouvert, avec une extension possible de 26 semaines.
x.interet: L'étude pourrait appuyer l'accès à l'anakinra pour les patients japonais atteints de maladie de Still. Elle apporte aussi des données de tolérance prolongée de l'anti-IL-1 chez l'enfant et l'adulte.
x.profil: Des enfants (dès 8 mois) et des adultes japonais atteints de maladie de Still active (AJIs ou Still de l'adulte).
inclusion: Diagnostic d'AJIs (critères ILAR adaptés) ou de Still de l'adulte (Yamaguchi) selon l'âge au début
Au moins un épisode fébrile ≥ 38,0 °C dans la semaine précédant l'inclusion
Test de tuberculose négatif dans les 8 semaines
exclusion: Traitement antérieur ou en cours par anakinra ou autre anti-IL-1 (sauf canakinumab arrêté pour une autre cause que l'échec)
Traitements immunosuppresseurs ou biologiques récents selon des délais de sevrage définis
Infection active ou chronique (tuberculose, VIH, hépatite B ou C, Covid-19)
Atteinte hépatique, insuffisance rénale chronique de grade 4-5
Syndrome d'activation macrophagique présent ou datant de moins de 4 semaines

bras.traitement: Anakinra sous-cutané, 100 mg/jour (≥ 50 kg) ou 2 mg/kg/jour (< 50 kg)
Placebo de volume correspondant pendant 2 semaines, puis anakinra en ouvert

x.duree: Environ 54 semaines en phase centrale, jusqu'à 26 semaines d'extension en option
x.critere: Amélioration d'au moins 30 % par rapport à l'inclusion à la semaine 2 (avis du médecin, avis du patient ou des parents, articulations actives, articulations limitées, fonction physique CHAQ/SHAQ, CRP)
